races.name: Well Of Moate Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Earthwatch
runners_data.note: Consistent form at this trip on Good ground (four top-4 finishes from five similar-going runs), handled by Daniel King for Denis Gerard Hogan who is 2/32 in the 14-day window; though a natural hold-up type, the volume of rear-runners means he is likely to end up racing more prominently than ideal, which tempers his finishing-kick credentials.

runners_data.name: Calamint
runners_data.note: Showed ability in bumpers including a solid third on Good ground, but returns from 92 days off and steps up to hurdles for the first time; Adrian Murray sends her out with just one runner in the window, and the maiden hurdle context with her hold-up style and hurdling unknown makes her an each-way curiosity rather than a confident pace-shape pick.

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: A repeat placed-runner at this trip on Good ground (2/16f/GOO, 4/16f/GOO) who stays well enough, though Brian O'Connell's charge is at heart a hold-up horse and with the field carrying so many rear-oriented runners, his ability to get a clean run through traffic is the key variable — STYLE_FIT flags the positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Digby Bridge
runners_data.note: Completely unknown on form with no public history supplied, but Barry Connell sends out a lightly-raced five-year-old with Sean Flanagan in the plate — a strong jockey booking that must be noted; the UNKNOWN going and style tags make him a genuine wild card who could be anything.

runners_data.name: Facile Ocean
runners_data.note: Good recent form — placed in three of his last four on similar ground (2/19f/GOO, 3/19f/GOO, 2/18f/GOO) — and Eoghan Finegan's 5lb claim is a practical advantage at the weights; his natural hold-up style is compromised by redistribution, but his Good-ground placed record gives him a strong underlying profile if he can position smartly.

runners_data.name: First Ascent
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy, arguably the most significant jockey booking in this field, partners a Gordon Elliott inmate who has placed in his last three over hurdles at this approximate trip; his patient midfield style suits the anticipated controlled pace shape, and Kennedy's ability to place a horse late at the second-last flight is a tangible asset.

runners_data.name: Through The Storm
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and pace-map anchor, but arrives after a 580-day absence for David Harry Kelly, who has had no runners in the 14-day window; she sets the race shape regardless of her own winning chance, and the long layoff means there is real uncertainty about whether she retains the ability or fitness to control proceedings.

runners_data.name: Whoyougonnacall
runners_data.note: Consistent if unspectacular form (3/18f/GOO, 4/16f/GOO) for John Patrick Ryan, who has 0 wins from 21 in 14 days, suggesting the trainer's runners need to run into form; naturally prominent and likely to sit just behind Through The Storm, which is the ideal tactical position if the pace is controlled.

runners_data.name: Not In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Debuts under Simon Torrens for Aidan Anthony Howard with no public form available and a headgear flag suggesting some behavioural consideration; as with Digby Bridge, the utter absence of data means she cannot be mapped reliably and must be treated as an unknown quantity who could outclass the field or struggle equally.

runners_data.name: Anns Getaway
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse who fades in the finish, adding a specific caution beyond just running-style redistribution; 140 days off for an amateur-ridden runner with zero wins or places from a small sample and flagged fading tendencies makes her hard to support even in a weak maiden hurdle, regardless of the race shape.

runners_data.name: Rose Mountain
runners_data.note: A horse who has finished out of the frame in all three hurdle starts on Good ground, including a pulled-up run, and is flagged as fading in the finish; Martin Hassett is 0/3 over 14 days, and nothing in the profile — form, style, jockey, trainer — points to a competitive showing here.

races.paceDynamic: Through The Storm is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner maiden hurdle, having shown prominent tendencies in both career starts, and with a 580-day absence there is genuine uncertainty about how aggressively John Shinnick will deploy her from the front — but she is the only horse mapped at lead and is likely to set a sustainable, uncontested rhythm on Good ground. Whoyougonnacall is the natural companion for the prominent berths, though the field contains a cluster of genuine hold-up types — Earthwatch, Facile Ocean, Anns Getaway, and Captain Hanley — who are redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply more hold-up inventory than the rear can accommodate; of these, Facile Ocean and Earthwatch are most likely to actually press forward and contest prominent positions. With one controlled pace-setter and Good ground at Kilbeggan, the race is set to be run at a measured tempo that will not sufficiently string out the field, meaning horses who can travel in midfield and produce a clean jump-to-jump round before asserting from the second-last will be advantaged — this shape firmly favours prominent-to-midfield gallopers with tactical fluency and reliable jumping, not true hold-up horses relying on a late finishing burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Through The Storm dictates an honest but sustainable gallop and the race is decided by horses travelling prominently into the straight.
scenarios.body: Through The Storm sets an uncontested tempo, the field remains compact through the back straight, and a horse positioned in the first four or five at the top of the home straight produces a clean jump at the last to assert; this is the dominant shape because there is only one pace-setter and Good ground rewards economical, prominent racing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely steady enough to compress the field and a sharp jumper picks up from mid-division two out.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling tempo means the race is not truly truly run until the home turn, compressing the field to the point where a horse from fifth or sixth that jumps slickly at the final two flights can sprint past the leaders; First Ascent or Earthwatch, both capable of sustaining an effort from midfield, are the profiles who benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Surprise Lands
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unknown runners — Digby Bridge or Not In A Hurry — arrives with superior bumper or flat ability and makes its class tell on a first hurdle start.
scenarios.body: An unexposed horse with untapped potential can bypass the experience deficit on a flat, right-handed 2m track like Kilbeggan where jumping rhythm matters more than battle-hardened form; the steady pace produced by Through The Storm suits a newcomer travelling easily in rear-to-midfield before unleashing a clean run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Through The Storm, despite her long absence, rediscovers form and is permitted to coast in front at such a generous clip that no rival can close.
scenarios.body: A truly uncontested lead at a pace that does not overly tax Through The Storm through the early stages allows her to bank a big enough lead turning in that hold-up types redistributed to midfield are racing too far back to peg her back before the line.

watchPoints.text: Through The Storm's ability to control pace after 580 days off is the hinge of the entire race — if she loses the front or fades in the back straight, the race shape fragments and any scenario A prediction is invalidated.

Facile Ocean and Earthwatch are both true hold-up horses attempting to race more prominently than ideal; watch how they settle in the first half-mile, as traffic congestion mid-pack could compromise multiple runners with similar profiles.

First Ascent is partnered by Jack Kennedy, whose presence in this grade for Gordon Elliott demands attention — the jockey's ability to manoeuvre from midfield late is a specific threat to any prominent runner who idles after the last.

Digby Bridge and Not In A Hurry are both completely unexposed, and strong jockey bookings (Sean Flanagan, Simon Torrens) on horses with zero public form should be treated as a live information gap — market moves at post time will be the only reliable signal.

Anns Getaway and Rose Mountain both carry fade warnings and weak recent form; in a maiden hurdle with compressed pace, a false pitch of early speed from either late in the race could interfere with legitimate contenders approaching the second-last.

races.name: Kieran Kelly Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Liceo
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with three placings from five runs on Good ground, including a third at this trip; trainer McLoughlin has had no winners in the last 14 days from five runs, but the 25-day turnaround is fine and the tongue-tie is retained — genuine hold-up type who needs the field to open up.
runners_data.comment: Liceo has placed third twice in his last four starts and returns after 25 days in good heart, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the chief concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter and Jack Kennedy is a major asset; one win and three places from eight Good-ground starts suggest this trip and surface suit, though the STYLE_FIT flag highlights it is racing in an atypical lead role — if it can replicate that effort, the uncontested lead is enormously valuable.
runners_data.comment: Blue Reed showed a second two starts back before winning three starts back, so ability is there, but a seventh last time out is a concern; he has distance and going experience to call on, though carrying 160 lb against a field of 14 looks a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: Progressive five-year-old with back-to-back second-place finishes on Good ground at 16-17f; ran just five days ago which is worth monitoring for fatigue, but Michael Kenneally's claim is attractive and the hood is retained — a genuine hold-up runner who has placed consistently at similar trips.
runners_data.comment: Placed second two of his last three starts, Syosset clearly finds a way into contention, yet he remains winless in recent starts and a trainer currently without a return from 25 runners gives little confidence; 160 lb is another ask.

runners_data.name: Valsorpresa
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a 15/15 sim-going record on Good, including one win and three places; however, this is a true hold-up type whose natural position will be surrendered in a field this size, and the 0/0 trainer-14-day blank adds limited confidence — the style displacement is real.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Valsorpresa nevertheless shapes as a genuine threat — he has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 96 puts him among the sharpest in here after 18 days off. The risk is that recent finishes suggest he has yet to fully convert that ability.

runners_data.name: Walk Win
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who found 2nd at 16f on Good last time, but the ⚠ finishing fade flag is a concern in a race that could play to hold-up horses; trainer Burke has minimal recent runners and the 33-day absence is manageable — positional style makes this one to follow closely early.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Walk Win at least shaped with promise when second three starts back, though unplaced efforts either side temper expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, returns after 33 days, but 159 lb is a stern ask off a mark of 94.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with a form string largely built over shorter flat distances (9-12f), and the step up to 16f hurdles on Good looks like a significant unknown; no sim-going wins or places at 2m+ suggest this is a speculative entry.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a pair of sevenths his best recent offerings, Folk Warrior faces a stiff ask carrying 158 lb and our rating of 72 leaves him well held on figures against this field.

runners_data.name: Convincing
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose recent form is entirely over shorter distances (8-10f) — stepping up to 2m hurdles is a big ask, and the trainer's 0/23 runners in the last 14 days is a loud booking; the STYLE_FIT flag compounds the concern here.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last three starts, Convincing returns after 17 days carrying 155 lb, and with connections in a cold spell of 0 from 23, this unexposed gelding needs more to suggest a turnaround is imminent.

runners_data.name: Zaryagle
runners_data.note: Ran just one day ago which is an immediate red flag; form figure of P and 11th over 20f on Good last time suggests modest ability at this trip, and the STYLE_FIT flag means the horse is unlikely to occupy its natural position — extreme caution warranted.
runners_data.comment: Rated 97 and ranked third of 14, Zaryagle has run over today's trip and going and is better than his recent finishes suggest, enough to make him a live threat at the weights carrying 154 lb — though winless in his last five and back out just one day ago, fitness and consistency are the main concerns.

runners_data.name: Corkbeg
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose best recent form came over longer trips (20-24f), and dropping to 2m may not fully suit; 14/15 sim-going record on Good is a positive for surface, but the hold-up nature mapped further forward than natural means tactical options are compromised.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Corkbeg does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 23 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; yet his two most recent efforts — ninth and seventh — make a big ask of him carrying 152 lb from eighth in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Ferdia
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran whose last five runs are all over 19-24f — this 2m looks a genuine trip short of optimum; no wins on Good from eight runs and all five recent finishes outside the places paint a difficult picture regardless of redistribution.
runners_data.comment: Ferdia has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating puts him clear of this field, but his recent sequence of a seventh, eighth, sixth, ninth and a pull-up leaves him winless in his last five starts — hard to trust despite the rating edge.

runners_data.name: Bravemans Bounce
runners_data.note: Four-year-old returning from an 85-day break with no wins from three runs, all finishing 8th or worse; the ⚠ fades flag and the STYLE_FIT displacement to midfield from a true hold-up profile make this one to treat with caution on comeback.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts — including an eighth and ninth — and returning after 85 days off, Bravemans Bounce faces a stiff ask carrying 151 lb; experience over today's trip and going is the one genuine plus, but our rating of 65 flags him as well held on current form.

runners_data.name: Kinski
runners_data.note: 118-day absence is the headline concern here — that layoff combined with a solitary sim-going placing from five Good runs and the ⚠ finishing fade flag suggests the horse needs the run; the STYLE_FIT displacement only adds to the lack of obvious angle.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Kinski is yet to win in recent starts and brings a concerning refusal last time out, returning after 118 days off carrying 151 lb — connections will need significant improvement on a patchy profile.

runners_data.name: Ardgillan
runners_data.note: Returning from 245 days off, making this effectively a seasonal reappearance; recent form figures (22nd, 13th, 9th) over similar trips paint a bleak picture, and the ⚠ fade flag alongside a 1/5 Good-ground record means it would need to show significant improvement.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, Ardgillan returns from a 245-day absence carrying 148 lb, yet to win in his last four starts but open to significant improvement as connections freshen him up for this test.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Lightly-weighted at OR 73 with a solid 14/15 sim-going record on Good and one win included — the application of the lowest weight in the field is an asset; naturally a hold-up type shifted forward by congestion, so a gap appearing late is the key requirement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of 14 on our figures, Surviving Murmansk is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 141 lb; a runner-up last time out is the one genuine plus, though frequent unplaced efforts before that temper enthusiasm considerably.

races.paceDynamic: Blue Reed is the sole confirmed front runner in a 14-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jack Kennedy can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m trip on Good ground at Kilbeggan. The race map is significantly congested at the rear: Valsorpresa, Convincing, Zaryagle, Corkbeg, Ferdia, Bravemans Bounce, Kinski, Ardgillan and Surviving Murmansk are all true hold-up types compressed into midfield because there is simply insufficient room for all of them to settle in their natural position — of these, Syosset and Liceo, with the clearest recent form and better tactical riders, are most likely to find a workable position closest to the pace. With Blue Reed able to bowl along at a fair but uncontested tempo, the race will likely develop into a steady-to-moderate-pace procession until the final bend where the field concertinas, placing a premium on a handy position and a horse that can travel into the race rather than grind from the back — this shape firmly favours hold-up horses who can be ridden prominently or those with the tactical nous to sit just off the lead, as pure closers starting their run from the rear will find it extremely difficult to thread through a compressed field over this sharp 2m trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blue Reed Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Reed is allowed to roll along uncontested and the pace remains controlled throughout, Kennedy can dictate every fraction and steal a march turning for home.
scenarios.body: Blue Reed settles into a rhythm, the field fans out behind, and Kennedy kicks approaching the last — having conserved energy through a moderate gallop, the front runner has enough in reserve to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two flights and a well-placed hold-up horse picks up sharply off the steady gallop.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up performer who has managed to find a workable mid-pack position — most likely Syosset or Liceo — tracks the front runner before delivering a sustained challenge at the last hurdle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Grabs It
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Reed weakens inside the final flight and a horse who has stalked close-up throughout swoops to lead on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Walk Win or Syosset, both with good recent Good-ground form at these distances, have the profile to be produced late from a prominent position to take advantage of a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compression Carnage — Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield causes interference or badly-placed horses find daylight late and the race is won from deep.
scenarios.body: The extreme pace compression means a well-handicapped runner like Surviving Murmansk or Corkbeg, who has found a gap late, could snatch a place from the chaos, though winning from the rear over a sharp 2m is a tall order given the redistribution of so many true hold-up types.

watchPoints.text: Blue Reed — monitor in the early furlongs: if Jack Kennedy is allowed a completely uncontested lead with no horse willing to press, the front runner could steal this race on a controlled pace that never truly tests its stamina.

Zaryagle — ran just one day ago and should be monitored for any signs of fatigue or sluggishness early; a horse running on consecutive days in a 14-runner handicap hurdle is a significant operational risk for those around it at jumps.

Syosset — ran only five days ago and faces a compressed midfield; if Michael Kenneally can find a clear passage early and sit just off Blue Reed, the recent form is strong, but the short turnaround over hurdles on a sharp track is worth watching at the first flight.

Ardgillan and Kinski — both returning from very long absences (245 days and 118 days respectively) in a busy 14-runner hurdle field; their unpredictability over hurdles after such breaks creates a potential jumping hazard, particularly at the early flights in a congested field.

Field compression in the back straight — with 13 horses mapped to midfield or hold-up positions behind a single front runner, the probability of crowding and checking on the bend is elevated; horses drawn to race wide or with bold jockeys capable of finding daylight early will have a material tactical edge.

races.name: Joe Cooney Memorial Hurdle

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by John Patrick Ryan (stable also saddles Pets Georgina) with form that reads as a stayer who plugs on late; sim-going record is modest (0W0P from 8 runs on Good) and the step to 3m1f is a positive, though finishing positions have been poor recently including a pull-up (P) in latest form.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up two outings back are obvious concerns, but Drumgill has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 129 gives him a live each-way claim; a trainer running at 0/21 in the last 14 days is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Olympic Man
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has not won in 15 sim-going runs (0W1P) and is 9 years old with a patchy recent record including a fall (F) and two unfinished runs; the 5lb claimer lightens the load but this horse faces a stiff task at OR 130 if it gets into a fight for the lead with the classier Rocky's Diamond.|
runners_data.comment:
Winless in his last five starts and with a trainer currently without a winner in 14 days, the risks are real — yet he has experience over today's trip and going, our rating of 132 ranks him second of the five, and 29 days off gives connections time to plot a revival.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Diamond
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 148 carrying 156lbs with a hot trainer at 3/7 over 14 days; has Good-ground form and experience stepping up from shorter trips, though recent form string (466-0P) shows a pull-up last time and the 10-day turnaround bears scrutiny — the trainer's form stat suggests confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Rocky's Diamond has run over today's trip and going, and at 156 lb he asks plenty of questions after a pull-up ten days ago — yet he remains the top-rated runner here and, winless in his last five starts notwithstanding, looks the one to beat on our assessment.

runners_data.name: Rememberwhat
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 6-year-old with only two hurdles runs on record, both on Good ground; limited data (2 hist runs, 0W0P) makes this horse difficult to assess with confidence, but the step up to 3m1f is a significant test for a lightly-raced type and the 7lb claimer Cian Cullinan takes the ride.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts, finishing sixth and fourth, Rememberwhat looks up against it here ranked last on our figures; he does have experience of today's going, though at 152 lb that weight burden makes a turnaround tough to envisage.

runners_data.name: Pets Georgina
runners_data.note: Strong sim-going record (2W3P from 6 runs on Good) and recent back-to-back wins including a 3m hurdle victory underline her affinity for this trip and surface; the hold-up style suits the expected contested pace dynamic perfectly, and J J Slevin — one of the leading jump jockeys — is a significant booking.|
runners_data.comment: Pets Georgina arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, giving her some hope of completing a hat-trick 22 days fresh — though a trainer cold streak of 0 from 21 over the past fortnight is the one cloud over her claims.

races.paceDynamic: Rocky's Diamond and Olympic Man are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 3m1f trip at Kilbeggan, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a dawdle. Rocky's Diamond arrives on the back of a sharp 10-day turnaround under an in-form trainer (3/7 T14) and is the classier of the two at OR 148, making it likely to set the terms with Olympic Man pressing and applying pressure through the middle stages. Drumgill and Pets Georgina are both hold-up types who will be waiting on the pace, while Rememberwhat from a prominent position fills the space between the leaders and the closers. The contested gallop over a stamina-testing 3m1f trip on Good ground strongly favours horses with a hold-up or late-running profile who can conserve energy and pounce on a tiring leader, with Pets Georgina's recent winning form at this sort of trip on Good ground making her the archetypal beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond and Olympic Man fight for supremacy and burn each other out, leaving the hold-up horses with a weakening leader to pick off in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a genuine gallop over 3m1f and begin to tire in the final half-mile on Good ground, opening the door for the hold-up horses to come through. Pets Georgina, a recent double winner on Good going over this trip range, and Drumgill, who has shown staying ability, are ideally profiled to absorb the pace and finish past flagging rivals.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Rocky's Diamond Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond bowls along at a controlled tempo, seeing off Olympic Man early and dictating a sustainable gallop that suits its jumping rhythm.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Diamond, the highest-rated runner at OR 148 and with an in-form trainer behind it, asserts over Olympic Man within the first mile and settles into a rhythm that negates the stamina demands. A class-based front-running performance at a manageable tempo could see it hold on against the closers, as its superior rating gives it a fitness and ability edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not brutal and Rememberwhat is able to travel prominently throughout without expending excess energy.
scenarios.body: Rememberwhat, prominent by style, tracks the leaders at a comfortable distance and benefits if the front-runners slow fractionally in the final mile rather than fully collapsing, allowing a prominent position to convert into a winning one. The horse's two runs both show placed form on Good going and a step up to 3m1f could suit if stamina holds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart through jumping errors, fallers, or a frenetic early pace that leaves all front-runners emptied out before the final flight.
scenarios.body: A messy, high-casualty race over an extended trip can occasionally produce a survivor rather than a winner, with hold-up horses benefiting most when the field fragments. Drumgill, who has experience of surviving over long trips even when finishing out of the frame, could pick through the wreckage, while Pets Georgina's jumping soundness gives her another route to the prize in attrition conditions.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rocky's Diamond and Olympic Man at the early hurdles — if they clash hard for the lead in the first mile, both risk running themselves into the ground, making the race wide open for closers before halfway.
Drumgill's recent pull-up (P in latest form) is a flag over this 3m1f trip; if the horse travels poorly in the rear watch for an early signal from Daniel King that it may not complete.

Olympic Man's age (9), recent fall, and zero wins from 15 sim-going runs makes it vulnerable if pressed by Rocky's Diamond — monitor whether the claimer O'Sullivan can settle it once headed rather than letting it fight a losing battle.

Rememberwhat's inexperience (only 2 career runs) over a 3m1f trip should be tracked at the midpoint of the race — if the young horse starts to paddle or lose its jumping rhythm, its prominent position could become a liability rather than an asset.

Pets Georgina's stable companion Drumgill could affect her run if both hold-up horses get boxed in together behind a slow-moving traffic jam — watch the early position of both Ryan-trained runners to see if they secure clean runs on the outside or get caught tight.

races.name: Smiddys Pub Mullingar Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Kings Jet
runners_data.note: Held-up operator who has struggled for consistency recently (form: 62P-U0), but has placed twice in similar going and distance ranges and runs fresh on just 6 days since last start; Ricky Doyle rides, and headgear (hood/pricker) is noted — needs the race to develop into a true staying test late to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Kings Jet is our top-rated runner and steps out just six days after his latest start, carrying 166 lb on going he has experience of. A second four starts back offers a crumb of form in a winless recent spell, but his rating of 110 makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Anodandawink
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at 162lbs with a sharp recent form line (03-921) including a win 17 days ago, this 5-year-old holds strong course-going credentials with five runs on Good (1W, 3P); Peter Smithers claims 7lbs, which is meaningful at this level — the fade-in-finish flag is worth watching, though at 3m1f the question is whether that tendency manifests or whether the extra stamina test suits.|
runners_data.comment: Anodandawink arrives on the back of a win last time out, and he has run over today's distance and going before, making him a clear danger under a rating of 92; the worry is a trainer who has drawn a blank in 23 attempts over the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Consistent stayer with form figures of 31-663 and nine runs on Good ground (1W, 3P), but genuinely a hold-up horse running from a midfield slot in this shape because the rear is congested — Simon Torrens rides for Rothwell, and the tongue-tie/pricker headgear signals a horse that can switch off; its chance is tempered if it cannot settle to its preferred deep position.|
runners_data.comment: Mistyburn brings experience of today's trip and conditions and was a winner four starts back, with a third last time out suggesting he retains some form — the concern is that his recent record includes two sixths, and he carries 148 lb.

runners_data.name: Zolpharine
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back on Good ground most recently (form: 505-11) and arrives on 71 days off, which makes the fitness angle worth monitoring; Daniel King rides for John Patrick Ryan, and while this horse's natural closing style is constrained by being mapped to midfield, those recent wins show it can still produce when conditions are right — a genuine place threat if it travels fluently.|
runners_data.comment: Zolpharine has back-to-back wins on his CV and has run over today's trip and going, but a 71-day absence, a struggling trainer without a winner in 21 recent attempts, and our rating 11lb below his official mark make him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old prominent racer shown on the lead because no confirmed front-runner exists in this field, not because it is a natural pace-setter — Michael Kenneally claims 5lbs; form reads PPPP-3 with the sole completion a third over 25f on Good, and its Good-ground record of 6 runs for 0 wins suggests finishing in front is the challenge; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.80 is the key caveat here.|
runners_data.comment: The Little Yank shaped with promise when third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 97 marks him out as a live danger; the four pulls-up in recent starts are a concern that's hard to ignore.

races.paceDynamic: The Little Yank, a natural prominent racer redistributed to the lead due to the absence of any confirmed front-runner, will set the pace over this 3m1f trip at Kilbeggan on Good ground — but does so out of role, making the tempo likely to be measured and sustainable rather than pressured. With four hold-up types behind him, the race will develop steadily through the early and middle stages, with horses conserving energy before the race quickens in the final mile. The field actually holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Zolpharine and Mistyburn are genuine closers who have been mapped to midfield because they cannot all settle as deep as they would naturally prefer. This uncontested, moderate-tempo scenario most favours horses who can travel prominently or make a smooth mid-race move, with a well-judged hold-up run from a horse capable of finding a strong finishing effort on Good ground the primary beneficiary profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If The Little Yank sets an uncontested, honest gallop and the race is run at a consistent, moderate tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: The Little Yank rolls along in front without pressure, setting a genuine but unhurried pace that strings the field out into the final straight; horses who have been travelling smoothly behind and can produce a sustained finishing effort are handed the advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If The Little Yank dictates fully, the pace proves too slow for closers to reel in, and the field fails to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: Racing against his natural style but uncontested, The Little Yank dictates every yard and, on Good ground over a trip where he has placed, simply outstays rivals who are outrun from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Overwhelm
scenarios.trigger: If Zolpharine or Mistyburn travel far more fluently than their redistributed map positions suggest and produce powerful closing runs.
scenarios.body: With the pace steady and the hold-up horses unable to fully settle to their natural rhythm, a horse that finds a slicker jumping round and a better berth than expected can sweep late; Zolpharine's back-to-back wins on Good ground make this plausible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the field materially or the pace collapses, causing a scrambled finish with no horse able to assert.
scenarios.body: With an 11-year-old in The Little Yank and a runner showing recent P-P-P-P form setting the gallop, a faltering tempo or multiple mid-race incidents could produce an untidy, scrappy finish; the horse with the most consistent jumping and freshest legs benefits.

watchPoints.text: Anodandawink carries a "fades in finish" flag — watch whether the 3m1f trip and a tendency to weaken late combine to cost it a winning position after travelling prominently for much of the race.
Zolpharine arrives on 71 days off; watch its condition paddock-side and early jumping — if it takes time to warm up, its natural hold-up role in a slow-run race could leave it with too much to do.

The Little Yank is an 11-year-old operating out of its natural prominent style; watch for any signs of a slow early jump or reluctance to stride on, which would remove the only pace-setter and leave the race in tactical limbo.

Mistyburn and Zolpharine are both genuine hold-up types squeezed into midfield on the map — watch the first few fences to see whether either can actually drop back and travel in its natural comfort zone, which would materially change the race shape from what is projected.

With Good ground confirmed across all seven races on the card and no change in going reports, watch for consistent jumping and ground-holding form to be rewarded — horses with multiple positive sim-going runs (Anodandawink 5/9, Mistyburn 9/15) hold a surface edge over those with sparser Good-ground records.

races.name: KEPAK Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Jasko Des Dames
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race, Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old has solid Good-ground form and is well-placed at OR 130 to dictate from the front; the STYLE_FIT flag notes it may be racing slightly out of role at this trip, so watch for any signs of pressure eroding its lead late.
runners_data.comment: Jasko Des Dames arrives here with experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 137 puts him clear at the head of this field. A second five starts back underpins his quality, and 22 days between runs suggests he comes here fresh; he's winless in recent starts, but this is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Ma Jacks Hill
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride on Gordon Elliott's six-year-old, a horse who has won twice at 20f on Good ground and boasts a strong course record — a genuine prominent racer whose trainer is in form (1/43 over 14 days) and who represents the classiest combination in the race.
runners_data.comment: Ma Jacks Hill won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing he retains the class to threaten at this level, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the chief concern is a trainer firing at just 2% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: A Law Of Her Own
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's nine-year-old is a natural hold-up performer with an exceptional Good-ground record (14 from 15 qualifying runs placed) and a recent win at 16f; only 8 days since last run but that freshness has not blunted her previously and she profiles as one of the best-suited runners to this shape.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back but unseated last time out, and that jumping frailty is the obvious concern for A Law Of Her Own; she has run over today's trip and going, and 159 lb is no easy task, though her form profile gives her every right to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Intense Approach
runners_data.note: A prominent-style runner with blinkers for John McConnell, whose trainer has gone 0/25 in the 14-day window — form figures read poorly (5U50-0) but four of five qualifying Good-ground runs produced placed efforts; the 8-day turnaround and recent run of zeros make it hard to trust at a short price.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and part of a trainer mired at 0/25 in the past fortnight, Intense Approach nonetheless ranks second of eight on our figures and has run over today's trip and going — the main risk is that elusive recent form simply continues.

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: J J Slevin partners Denis Hogan's eight-year-old, whose true style is front-prominent but the field density means it cannot realistically hold that berth — its best form has come when racing in the first two or three, and being shuffled back compromises its chance meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Mickie Angel looks hard to fancy here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out plus second two starts back show some consistency, but 156 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: The second McConnell runner, a nine-year-old hold-up horse wearing a hood, has a model profile for this shape: five of five qualifying Good-ground runs placed including two seconds, all at the trip, and Josh Williamson claims 5lb which brings the weight to a manageable 156lbs.
runners_data.comment: Rexem arrives here just eight days after finishing second two starts back, showing he's in good heart, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is a trainer who has gone 0/25 in the last 14 days, which is a red flag.

runners_data.name: Ceanndana
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's nine-year-old has been off 85 days, and while its form figures over 2-3m on Good ground are plentiful (13 from 15 qualifying runs placed), it is a prominent-style horse that the field shape forces into a midfield role it would not naturally choose — that positional compromise, combined with the layoff, limits its attractiveness here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of eight on our figures, Ceanndana hasn't run for 85 days and his trainer is without a win in 27 attempts over the past fortnight; he has experience over today's trip and going, but he's hard to fancy carrying 152 lb.

runners_data.name: Grange Walk
runners_data.note: At 11 years old and OR 106, Daniel King's partner for John Patrick Ryan is a genuine hold-up type wearing a hood — but the redistribution note confirms it has been slotted into a midfield position rather than its natural rear-of-field berth, and its record shows zero wins from 15 qualifying Good-ground runs, making it a place-at-best proposition at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and with a trainer yet to saddle a winner in 21 attempts over the past fortnight, Grange Walk faces a stiff ask here; the third three starts back offers some hope, but a recent fall complicates his profile.

races.paceDynamic: Jasko Des Dames is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger for the lead identified, should settle into an uncontested rhythm at Kilbeggan's straightforward circuit over 2m4f on Good ground — conditions that reward horses who can travel comfortably and jump fluently throughout. The pace is likely to be honest rather than frantic, giving Jasko Des Dames every chance to dictate margins and conserve energy for the final climb. This shape suits hold-up horses who can track the tempo and pounce late, as well as prominent racers who slot in just behind the leader and improve into the straight — A Law Of Her Own and Rexem, both genuine hold-up types with strong Good-ground records, are ideally profiled. Three horses — Mickie Angel, Ceanndana, and Grange Walk — are displaced from their natural positions: Mickie Angel and Ceanndana are true prominent racers who cannot all hold that berth and are mapped to midfield, while Grange Walk is a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot, meaning none of the three are likely to race where they are shown and their chances in any shape that depends on those positions should be moderated accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jasko Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Jasko Des Dames gets a soft lead and controls tempo throughout without being pressured, jumping accurately to keep rivals honest.
scenarios.body: Jasko Des Dames sets a sustainable gallop from the front, never quickening so sharply as to blow up but making the race messy enough for closers to find traffic; horses travelling prominently just off the pace are best placed to attack the final fence with momentum already built.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and genuine hold-up performers can make ground smoothly from the final circuit.
scenarios.body: A Law Of Her Own, with strong recent Good-ground form including a course-distance win, is ideally suited to this shape, as is Rexem whose consistent place-form over this trip on Good ground marks it as a reliable finisher.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Jasko Des Dames sets too fast an early tempo and weakens sharply after the last, allowing midfield runners to pour past.
scenarios.body: Mickie Angel and Ceanndana, though mapped to midfield rather than their natural prominent position, could benefit from a bunched finish if the leader stops — but both are racing out of role here, capping confidence in this shape materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl, Sprint Home
scenarios.trigger: If Jasko Des Dames sets a very slow early tempo that compresses the field and produces a dash from the final fence.
scenarios.body: A messy, sprint-like finish over these obstacles at Kilbeggan on Good ground tends to suit the horse with the most residual class and a jockey able to manufacture a run — Ma Jacks Hill with Jack Kennedy aboard fits that profile, though a crawl is the least likely tempo outcome given the field size.

watchPoints.text: Jasko Des Dames settles into a fully uncontested lead — if Mike O'Connor is allowed to dictate every yard of the pace with no challenger, the race shape dramatically compresses and hold-up horses are left with far less ground to make up than their style requires.

Mickie Angel and Ceanndana may both attempt to push forward early despite being mapped to midfield — if either forces its way to a prominent pitch, the early tempo could quicken and expose Jasko Des Dames to more pressure than the PACE_DYNAMIC anticipates.

A Law Of Her Own ran only 8 days ago and comes back quickly; watch the market to see whether Emmet Mullins has her at peak readiness, as a hold-up horse who fails to travel sweetly on this tight circuit will struggle to produce a late run.

Rexem is partnered by a 5lb claimer (Josh Williamson) — at a course like Kilbeggan where jumping fluency and positioning at fences matters, any inexperience at the obstacles over 2m4f could cost the horse its natural rhythm at a critical stage.

The final race-by-race going reports all confirm Good throughout the card at Kilbeggan — the surface has not deteriorated through the evening, meaning early-race form lines on this ground are valid comparators and no late softening bias should be applied.

races.name: Connellan & Noone Solicitors LLP Longford Flat Race

runners_data.name: Confidence Within
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Confidence Within was third last time out — his only recent start — and returns after 97 days off carrying 168 lb, yet to score but interesting on limited evidence.

runners_data.name: Srah
runners_data.comment: Srah ran seventh last time out and remains yet to win, but with just one run on record he is deeply unexposed and open to significant improvement; the yard is enduring a cold spell, and he shoulders 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Hot Rock Harry
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last two starts, Hot Rock Harry is lightly raced and remains open to improvement; the trainer's yard is in a lean spell, and he shoulders a hefty 165 lb burden here.

runners_data.name: Inishtearaght
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Inishtearaght nonetheless rates as the one to beat on these terms, having run over today's trip and going before; carrying 165 lb is a stiff ask, but his rating heads the field of six.

runners_data.name: Mr Enigma
runners_data.comment: Mr Enigma is lightly raced and unexposed, with a third last time out suggesting he is open to improvement; returning after 35 days and carrying 165 lb, he has done little wrong in recent starts and could progress further.

runners_data.name: Appy Ways
runners_data.comment: Appy Ways makes her racecourse debut here carrying 158 lb, and with no public form to go on she arrives as a completely unexposed unknown — lightly raced connections could have anything on their hands.
